findings.where: Nav bar, 'Destinations' link (desktop inline, and inside the phone Menu), and the 'MantaHostels home' wordmark link
findings.fault: The parts map has 'Destinations' going to a #destinations fragment that does not exist on this page, so a click does nothing. The wordmark's home link goes back to this same page. A visitor who has read how ranking works and now wants to look at hostels in Bali or Lombok has no working way off the page to the hostels or to home.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker choosing where to stay. This page exists so they trust the ranking enough to go and use it, and every route to that ranking is a dead end.

findings.fault: According to the parts map, all three link back to this page and not to the privacy policy, the terms or a way to report content. They look like real links, so a click that only reloads 'How we rank' looks broken.
findings.who_objects: A careful first-time visitor checking who runs the site before trusting a new, unknown platform. On a page whose whole job is trust, a privacy link that goes nowhere has the opposite effect. A hostel owner who wants to report a listing has no route either.

findings.where: The 'Hostelworld, for comparison' section (h2 and paragraph) at the end of the page
findings.fault: The page gives a section heading to a named competitor and sets up a head-to-head comparison of review mechanics. That is the competing-and-naming the positioning rules out ('the durable claim names no competitor', never anchor on review policing), and it does so while the Hostelworld affiliate consent is still pending. The paragraph also never draws its conclusion. It ends with 'can look thin there' and leaves the visitor to work out what Manta does differently.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because this is a competitor callout the product brief keeps off the site while the #78 consent is open. The backpacker, who reaches the last section and gets a dense one-sentence account of another site's rules with no takeaway for their own choice.

findings.where: Page end, after the Hostelworld paragraph (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page ends on body text with no next step: nothing like 'see hostels in Bali' or 'browse destinations'. The only way on is to scroll back up to the nav or down to the footer.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker, who has just been persuaded the ranking is fair and now has to hunt for where to use it. That is friction at the moment they are most ready to move on.

findings.where: Opening block: the lede, the summary sentence and the three-item numbered list, followed by the first paragraph of 'Ranking method'
findings.fault: The key takeaways (no paid placement, recent stays count more, few reviews start near the area average) are in small body type and look just like the body text, so a skimmer cannot tell this is the summary. The page then repeats the same points: 'No hostel can pay for a higher position' appears in the list and again as the first line of the next section. The lede spends its first line on 'instead of calling it proprietary', which answers a debate the visitor never had, and never says what this means for them.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone mid-trip who will read only the first screen. The three facts they came for carry no more weight than the paragraphs, and the repetition makes the page feel longer than it is.

findings.where: Body copy throughout 'Ranking method', 'Scoring method' and 'Hostelworld, for comparison'
findings.fault: The paragraphs are long, dense, single sentences with insider terms such as 'partner tier', 'listing presence', 'weighted count of recent reviews', 'direct booking exit' and 'minimum number of reviews is never a default filter'. Some sentences run past 60 words, the Hostelworld paragraph is essentially one sentence, and 'Both would bury exactly the low-review properties that pulling thin scores toward the area average exists to rank fairly' needs two readings.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker reading on a phone, often on a poor connection and in transit. They wanted 'can I trust the order?' and got a methods appendix. Many will give up before the parts that answer them.

findings.fault: The method is described but never shown. There is no example of the score chip ('8.9 · Great · 214 reviews'), no explanation of the Loved/Great/Solid/Mixed words, and no picture of the reward-code badge or of 'No reviews yet'. The text names these things, but the visitor cannot link them to what they will see on a listing. With no illustration or brand moment either, the page reads as a terms document.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because 'sterile/corporate is the named enemy' in the brand brief. The backpacker, who will meet a score chip and a badge on a listing and not recognise them as the things this page explained.

findings.where: Ranking and scoring sections, compared with the footer line 'Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali'
findings.fault: Everything is in the present tense, as if listings, scores, badges and reward codes are already live ('a hostel shows a full score', 'a reward-code badge … is the only signal on the page'). The only sign that the product is pre-launch is a small muted line in the footer.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor who goes looking for ranked hostels and badged reviews that do not exist yet. They will feel misled, which undoes the trust this page is trying to build.

findings.where: Desktop layout: the content column against the right side of the page and the footer
findings.fault: The text sits in a narrow column on the left, about 520 px wide, and the right 60% of the 1440 px screen is empty sand from top to bottom. The footer below is centred, so the page has two different axes and looks unfinished, as if a sidebar failed to load.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor planning their trip. The lopsided page and the change of alignment in the footer make it look like a draft, not a finished product.

findings.fault: Both lists are numbered. The intro's three items are unordered principles, not steps, so the numbers suggest a sequence or ranking that does not exist. The scoring percentages would be easier to compare as a short table of age against weight.
findings.who_objects: A skimming reader, who may read '1. No hostel can pay' as step one of a process.

findings.where: Footer: the 'MantaHostels' wordmark, and the link row at phone width
findings.fault: The footer wordmark is static but uses link colours, so it looks like a home link and a click does nothing. At phone width the link row wraps after 'How we rank ·', which leaves a separator dot hanging at the end of the first line.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who taps the footer logo expecting to go home, the usual pattern, and gets nothing. The stray dot is minor polish a designer would notice.
